correctness.rationale: Every nonconstant Walsh character has squared norm N on the vertex space; each sign-crossing undirected edge contributes 4w to its energy. Parity and the mean singleton quotient give the two unrestricted upper bounds 4W1/N and 4(W1+2W2)/(dN). For t<2 their crossing is the unique maximum of their minimum under W1+tW2=1, giving the asserted totals and value; for t≥2 the mean singleton bound is at most 4/(dN), strictly smaller if t>2 and W2>0. Uniform conductance c=4/[Nd(2+(d−1)t)] on both shells attains the lower-price bound because the Walsh eigenvalue of weight k is 2c k(d−k+1)≥2cd; uniform ordinary cube edges attain the high-price bound. Above t=2 equality forces every singleton to be a minimum eigenvector on the mean-zero space, giving 2 w_{x,x+e_i}=Γ at each vertex and hence edgewise uniqueness. In the invariant subclass, Walsh eigenvalues are twice the cut weights of the coordinate graph with auxiliary vertex 0, edge weights w_0i=b_i and w_ij=a_ij. Equality at singleton cuts yields b_i+Σ_j a_ij=q=Γ/2; eliminating b_i makes λ_S=2q(|S|−Σ_{ij⊂S}z_ij) for z_ij=2a_ij/q. Thus cut lower bounds give exactly the subset forest inequalities, and b_i≥0 gives degree bounds. These induced-subset inequalities also give the graphic-matroid rank inequalities for any edge subset by summing over its connected components. Parity equality fixes total z=d−1 below the threshold, giving budget Nq[2+(d−1)t]/4=1; at t=2 the budget is automatic from singleton equalities and total z need only be ≤d−1. A path on [d] gives a cycle on the augmented graph via its two endpoint edges to 0; all its d+1 classes are positive and attain the gap. Independent python3 /workspace/reproductions/2.py verifies 72 exact cut spectra and budgets, including a fractional slack forest at t=2 and prices on both sides. This tests designs and boundaries, not arbitrary-parameter optimality or a classification of nonsymmetric optimizers at t≤2.

evidence: The FMMP framework is broader on graph and prices and its standard SDP formulation (3) is directly applicable. Its inspected applications instead give a small explicit graph and path examples. Boyd et al.'s edge-transitive SLEM result gives a uniform optimum for that different objective; the general Turán framework uses positive-definite support and a linear sum objective.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The general FMMP formulation and optimality machinery are prior; they pose the exact problem but do not solve the cube equality conditions. Unpriced edge-transitivity and Turán bounds do not give the price transition or the constrained forest face. No whole-paper comparison is claimed for the limited Ghosh–Boyd access.

evidence: Mirafzal describes the unweighted adjacency spectrum and multiplicities of the same square graph, accounting for the spectral part of the all-edge-equal attaining design. Karlin–Lindqvist–Yao's title is closely related, but the DOI/full-text routes did not yield inspectable passages.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The fixed-weight spectrum does not exclude arbitrary edgewise designs; parity and singleton Rayleigh certificates and their equality conditions are the missing step. The SLEM optimum has stricter negative-eigenvalue control than the CT tree/forest classification; even overlap on a uniform optimizer does not imply the full theorem. Historical coverage by the inaccessible 1993 source was not determined.

evidence: Sun et al. exactly formulate positive price-weighted maximization of λ2 on a connected graph (and show the budget binds). arXiv:0709.0955 and Resultary 20328f74e74c optimize SLEM instead. For an optimal t<2 invariant design the common exit rate is q(d+1)/2 and the normalized marginals are those used in the two-hop stochastic comparison.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Normalizing by the constant exit rate does not turn continuous-time maximization of λ2 into minimizing an eigenvalue modulus. In d=5 the Hamilton-path design colors the augmented coordinate cycle alternately and the Walsh character with S={1,3,5} has normalized transition eigenvalue −1, so this priced CT optimizer is not a SLEM minimizer. The positive-definite shell problem concerns upper, not lower, cut constraints after Fourier transformation.

originality.rationale: The supported distinct claim is the solved price-dependent two-shell continuous-time problem and the tree/forest equality family, not the general FMMP optimization framework or the fixed unweighted square-cube spectrum. Closest indexed statements are distinguished by traceable objective, support, and optimizer comparisons. Historical risk remains for uninspected spectral/majorization work.
residual_risks: The closely titled 1993 Karlin–Lindqvist–Yao article and the full Ghosh–Boyd paper were not independently inspected in full; the former is the main priority risk. Access failure is not evidence of noncoverage.
Equivalent continuous-time design or extremal-cut statements may be known under another network-design or association-scheme formulation. The finite literature comparison is not proof of priority.

value.rationale: A single threshold settles when distance-two links help across an arbitrary-dimensional natural design family. The explicit tree/forest face gives more than the optimum value: it explains and certifies very sparse and fully dense exact solutions within the same price-normalized class. Above the threshold edgewise rigidity holds without a symmetry assumption. These distinctions are usable for design and are not just a change of parameters in the general SDP.
